intended_object: An accessor: given a compatible family z (a point of the library's inverse limit of finite membership-pattern stages), it reads the truth value of the coordinate U from the singleton stage {U}. Inferred from the docstring and from how the module uses it.
explanation: `Family X` is a library-internal construction. It assigns to each finite set of compact opens a membership pattern that some point of X realizes, compatibly under restriction to subsets. `coordinateValue` projects such a family to its value at a single compact open U, via the singleton stage {U}. Two lemmas check that it behaves as intended. `coordinateValue_toFamily` shows that for the family of a point x the value is `x ∈ U`. `stage_coordinate_iff_coordinateValue` shows that, by compatibility, the value is the same in every finite stage containing U. The body therefore matches its docstring. It is a technical projection used to reconstruct the space from finite pieces (motivated by Hochster's description), not a standard mathematical notion. It is already stated for an arbitrary topological space, so generality is not an issue, and Mathlib has no counterpart.
